sentences.text: This synthetic document describes the Cu–Pb binary system as calculated with pycalphad from the SGTE dataset CuPb-86Hay-LB.tdb; every figure, table and stated value is generated, and the exact values are kept in a separate truth key.
The highest invariant reaction, L1 → (Cu) + L2, lies at 956.8 °C.
The Cu–Pb system belongs to the 20 binaries of the ORCHID benchmark, chosen to cover diagram types such as miscibility gap, monotectic.
The thermodynamic description is the SGTE collection entry [1], which reproduces the assessment of F.H. Hayes, H.L. Lukas, G. Effenberg, G. Petzow, Z. Metallkd., 77, 749-54(1986). [2].
The calculations use pycalphad 0.11.2 at 1 atm.
The melting point of Cu reproduced by the dataset is 1084.6 °C.
At 956.8 °C the monotectic L1 → (Cu) + L2 takes place; the L1 phase then contains 22.2 at.% Pb.
The eutectic reaction L → (Cu) + (Pb) is calculated at 326.3 °C, with L at 99.8 at.%.
Table 1 compares the calculated temperatures with experimental values from the literature [3–5]; in this synthetic document those values and references are fictitious.
The upper stability limit of HCP_A3 is 327.5 °C.
The solubility of Cu in (Pb) reaches 50.0 at.% at 326.9 °C.
At 1450 K the integral mixing enthalpy of the liquid has its maximum, 6806 J/mol, at 48.0 at.% Pb.
The calculated enthalpy of formation of HCP_A3 at 298.15 K is 0.42 kJ/mol per mole of atoms.
Its heat capacity at room temperature is 25.86 J/(mol K).
For the equiatomic liquid at 1450 K, the Gibbs energy of mixing is −3.09 kJ/mol-atom.
In older units the corresponding mixing enthalpy is 1625 cal/mol (1 cal = 4.184 J).
This document is synthetic and exists only to test extraction tools; its truth key lists every boundary, field, invariant, plotted point, table cell and stated value.
